body: Split the shared-occupancy migration: TASK-032 migrates traffic sensing, junction grants, spawner and police lane use (enough for M1 + siren yield); walk avoidance, fire line, sight and conflict-point reservations go to follow-up TASK-036. Alternative rejected: migrate all five consumers now (fire line and sight already see cars, walk-avoidance symptom unconfirmed).
Verdict SUSPECT (not HOLDS): R1 146 s stander is held by the player standing in its lane, control moved the player out of the 90 m bubble; the other M1 sessions left unrefuted.

Shared occupancy = a per-tick flat snapshot resource (RoadOccupancy: footprints of every Vehicle and Character near the player, velocity, standing seconds, siren flag, manoeuvre claims) with strip/overlap queries, built by one system before traffic Drive and PoliceSystems. Alternative rejected: wrapping avian SpatialQuery only (cannot carry standing time, claims or the on-path rule, and would conflict with advance_traffic's mutable car query).

A passer's occupancy entry carries its committed pass envelope (claim) seen by opposite-direction queries, the spawner and grants into the opposite lane; commit needs the claim plus a comfortable-stop stretch (v0^2/2b + s0) clear. Alternative rejected: footprint-only passers, which deadlock head-on when an oncoming car appears mid-pass (both brake face to face; the passer beside the obstacle cannot merge back).

Traffic sensing uses two strips from the nose: one at the car's current lateral offset (length = the distance needed to finish the lateral move) and one at its target lateral; on-path kinematic cars stay skipped only for a car with no lateral move. Alternative rejected: dropping the kinematic skip for every car (a straight cast into a junction box would hit cars on non-conflicting connectors and brake queue heads, the TASK-033 gridlock class).

Remove the TASK-016 approach_clear pursuit spawn filter once sirens yield and police choose lanes; G6 (police close in 8/10 seeds, RED with yield and any-lane disabled) carries the decision. Alternative rejected: keep the filter, which would also reject most ahead and beside spawns (their lane route to the player crosses traffic).

An obstacle too close to the stop line for the pass to merge back is handled by an offset junction entry (the passer requests its connector from its lateral offset; conflicts computed geometrically on the actual offset path; lateral decays linearly along the connector). Alternative kept as the named fallback: the orchestrator's stuck-car despawn cheat off frame.

Offset junction entry restricted to the straight connector with a whole-box conflict set, instead of PLAN.md D4 geometric conflicts on a shifted polyline (alternative: keep D4 geometry; rejected: sign-error risk and SUMO allows opposite-direction driving only over straight links).

Police lane offsets [-1.0] applied in Respond and Chase with a corridor-strip IDM from RoadOccupancy, instead of [-0.7,-1.0,1.0] in Respond only with the heading cast (alternative rejected: -0.7 w leaves 0.30 m to a yielded row and the heading cast stalls the car into a dismount).
Pass claims derived in snapshot_road from TrafficCar.manoeuvre plus immediate insert on commit, instead of set_claim at the end of advance_traffic (rejected: oncoming sensing never sees the claim).

connector_clear (D1) sees every AI car that holds no grant at the node, on-path kinematic ones included, and a connector_clear failure does not push the waiter into `blocking`. Alternative rejected: V2/PLAN body set 'Vehicle, Traffic, claims', which hides a D2-demoted on-path car standing on its connector and lets a conflicting waiter be granted through it (kinematic pass-through).

A committed pass holds its nose behind the committed obstacle (virtual standing obstacle at its rear) until |lateral| >= need; strip C length gets 2*min_gap instead of min_gap. Alternative rejected: V2 strip C length v*|d|/r + min_gap, which at rest equals IDM's rest gap, so the obstacle drops out of the strip and the passer drives into it (TASK-016 rest-point lesson).

Police lane choice returns to offset 0 on a tie (clear(0) >= clear(current)) after lane_hold_seconds; leaving 0 needs the lane_gain. Alternative rejected: PLAN's symmetric gain rule, which keeps a siren car in the oncoming lane whenever both strips are clear.

Bumped-car recovery keeps PLAN's hysteresis sweep predicate (skin 0.4, horizon 0.5) instead of the spec's literal 'no dynamic body within switch reach' (5 m). Alternative rejected: the literal 5 m rule never recovers a car whose nudging player car or on-foot player stays within 5 m, which makes G3(a) unreachable.

Stage 1 closed green: causes (a) left car seeds 1/7, (b3) dummy pressed at a Dynamic car's bumper, (c) character in lane, (d) car on a connector reproduce RED and are ignored until their stage; (b1) nudge, (b2) shoved to curb, (b4) yawed 45 deg do NOT reproduce (the Dynamic car drives on) and stay as green regression rows. G1 baseline on gridlock seeds 1/2/7/42: 0 violations, max depth 0.000 m. R1 (fixed script, player off the carriageway) is green on current code (leave max stand 9.2 s, control 10.2 s). Alternative rejected: building G3 rows for b1/b2/b4 as causes (they are not).

Stage 2 closed green: RoadOccupancy snapshot + strip/overlap queries; traffic sensing, lane start and spawner moved onto it; lateral law; G8 rows (sensing a/b/c, lane start, city lane facts) flip-RED by one combined sabotage build (skip Traffic in sense and lane start, drop Vehicle and Character bodies from the snapshot) and green after restore; gridlock asserts G1 (clean, 4 seeds). Gridlock drift reported: worst stand s1 18.8->26.4, s2 34.3->27.2, s7 18.0->18.1, s42 27.7->23.0 s (flat spawner check moves the TrafficRng stream). Benches unchanged (~1.62 ms). Alternative rejected: keeping the avian slab cast for Dynamic cars (it would stay blind to off-path kinematic cars).

Stage 3 closed green: recover_dynamic (upright, not lost, at rest, sweep hysteresis skin 0.4 / 0.5 s, sampled rejoin corridor) with give-up after recover.give_up_seconds standing IN Dynamic (new TrafficCar.stood; using the snapshot standing time gave up a car at once after a long kinematic stand and broke traffic_pedestrian). G3 a/c/d/e green, flips: (a) recover.seconds 1e6 RED; (c) hysteresis removed + corridor blind to dynamic bodies RED (7 switches, recovery and re-switch fall in one tick, so switches are counted from TrafficStats); (e) corridor reduced to the current pose RED. Cause b3 now green (given up -> Abandoned). Alternative rejected: the plan's (c) flip 'switch skin/horizon' (stays green: at contact both predicates block).

Go-around commit as planned (claim free of bodies AND a 45 m comfortable-stop stretch beyond it free of vehicles) starves on a busy street: seed 7 cause (a) head never commits in 120 s, the oncoming stream (spacing ~24 m < claim ~27 m + stretch 45 m) never leaves the gap. First failure of the class 'oncoming pass starves' (not pass-through, not head-on deadlock).

The pass claim is published at commit (Pass{go:false}) while the car still stands on its line; oncoming cars that are not yet inside the claim stop before it (claims straddling a strip origin are ignored, so a car already inside drives out); the passer shifts (go) once the claim holds no body. Commit needs no opposite claim and no standing body or character in the claim; the 45 m stretch check is dropped. Alternative rejected: keeping the stretch (never commits under continuous oncoming flow) and a separate request/reservation table (the orchestrator's 'no second bookkeeping' rule).

Pass hold rule 'nose holds at hold_s while |lateral| < need' also fired during the merge back (lateral drops below need past the obstacle): the passer froze half in the opposite lane and head-on stalls followed (cause (a) seed 1, 55-60 s stands). Fixed by holding only while s <= hold_s.

Go-around timing rules after the seed-1 head-on trace: an oncoming car ignores a claim it already straddles (it drives out); a published pass goes only when its claim holds no body AND no oncoming car beyond the claim end is closer than its hard-braking stop (v^2/2*max_decel + s0); a new pass does not commit while an oncoming AI car waits beyond the claim (alternation; abandoned/parked vehicles there do not count). trigger_gap 6 -> 10 m so the car right behind a head that moved out joins in tandem. Alternative rejected: a separate reservation/request table.

Stage 4 closed green: G2 10 rows (street/avenue x seeds 1/2/7/42, dummy seeds 1/7): first 8 queued cars pass within 7.7-49 s, worst stand <= 21.9 s, 0 passer contacts, G1 depth 0. Flips: pass.vehicle/character_seconds 1e6 -> not past + 143 s stands RED; passer typed OnPathTraffic + claims hidden -> G1 depth 2.4 m + contacts RED. G8 spawner row flip ClaimFilter::None RED. Causes (a)/(c) now judge cars queued behind the obstacle (a 60 m radius caught junction approaches held for room at the lane start, printed). Pass reaching the lane end (plan 4.2 step 6) not built: such a pass is refused.

Unconditional D2 (demote any holder on its connector/past the line standing for the lease while contested) churned walker-held holders on seed 1 (exit crosswalk mutual wait, 66 s approach stands); giving demoted holders first place again (stamp 0) re-granted them the same tick (23.6 s stale). D2 now demotes only holders whose path a standing non-walker body blocks (TASK-033 crosswalk rule kept).

Stop rule hit for the box class: cause (d) (car left mid-box at seed-1 node 83) still locks two approaches 99-113 s after D1-D3 (1st) and after D5 connector pass with whole-box grants and a whole-box lease (2nd): the box passer is switched Dynamic by a walker mid-pass and abandoned, leaving two bodies no pass fits around. Row (d) ignored with the reason; redesign note in IMPL_SUMMARY. No third patch.

Stage 5 closed (stop rule on (d)): D1 grants check the connector path (G8 junction row, flip RED); D2 demotion limited to body-blocked holders; D3 re-pick for queue heads and for a car at the start of its connector (same start pose); D5 box pass with whole-box grants (entry for heads whose every exit is blocked, lease on the whole box). G4 seeds 1/7 + extra row green; G4 D1-removed flip stays green in the city (the G8 row carries D1). Cars placed on a connector without a grant queue for it (traffic_idm fixture). Alternative rejected: third patch on the box pass.

Stage 5b (orchestrator redesign note): stuck cheat as a new Bubble system traffic/stuck.rs (before despawn_traffic): a traffic car, or a driverless non-police car in a junction box, standing and out of frame (in_frame, the bubble predicate) for bubble.stuck_despawn_seconds = 45 s despawns. 45 s sits above the 40 s TASK-033 stand bound so no liveness gate is masked. Cause (d) split: out-of-view row (stands <= 46 s, left car gone; flip limit x1000 RED 120 s) and in-view residue row (left car never despawned in frame; flip in_frame dropped RED). Alternative rejected: reusing the Offscreen counter of traffic cars (plain parked cars have none, and it does not reset on motion).

G6 on streets (orchestrator fallback 1: oncoming lane + oncoming yield built): 0/10 pressure with production traffic, 10/10 on the same routes with no traffic. Yielded rows on both curbs leave 1.7 m < 2.4 m; the police weaves at 2-5 m/s or stands until the yield timeout.

G6 on avenues (orchestrator fallback 2): 2/10 with traffic, 7/10 with no traffic at all (the Respond route slows to turn_speed in every box, lane choice is off in boxes). Stop rule: REDESIGN_NOTE.md with options; both G6 rows ignored with the note as reason. No third patch.

Kept four siren mechanism fixes found while diagnosing G6 (each gate green): lane_frame keeps the car's own lane when it is out in the opposite lane; lane choice compared from the tail over a speed-dependent horizon; no yield without a way past or within a car length of the lane start; yield_gap v^2/2b (the planned + s0 is IDM's rest point, the car crept forever) with shift-then-stop. Alternative rejected: reverting to the plan text (G5 cars never stopped, the siren car lost its frame in the opposite lane).

R1 runtime leave run is RED in 3/3 runs (11-15 traffic cars stand ~150 s within 45 m; control 0 over 20 s): the car left in the junction box in view is the stage-5 box class the orchestrator accepted as residue, and at the baseline spot (6.3, -84.6) it is worse than pre-TASK-032 (9.2 s): D1 refuses grants through the body and a car that touched it is given up (Abandoned) as a second body. Reported in REDESIGN_NOTE.md (options R-A push-through, R-B cheat at distance, R-C accept); no patch (box stop rule already hit).

Standing time in the road occupancy restarts when a body moved more than hold_speed x dt since last tick (a teleport or respawn keeps velocity 0): t15 seed 1 hijack failed because the teleported player counted as a person standing for minutes and the target car went around him at once. Alternative rejected: measuring the wait from the passer's side (a per-car hold timer; more state, same effect for real walkers). Gate: traffic_occupancy standing_restarts_after_a_teleport (flip: displacement check removed, RED).

G7 hidden rule for police car spawns: occlusion rays go to the four top chassis corners (same 4-ray budget) instead of population::occluded's head/width/feet rays; the gate's own corner check found 18 of 1920 spawns with a corner in view under the old rays. Alternative rejected: loosening the gate to the dispatcher's rays (then it would only restate the production predicate).

Rated the hijacked-mid-pass phantom claim MAJOR (oncoming lane freezes while the player drives the car: snapshot derives claims for Taken cars, on_hijack keeps manoeuvre) and required R-A to exclude characters and bodies past the box on the destination lane start. Alternative rejected: treating R-A as "any standing body at the box", which breaks traffic_intersection::abandoned_car_past_the_box_holds_no_car_inside (TASK-016 do-not-block-the-box) and would shove pedestrians.

R-A push through the box, attempt 1: loose (driverless, non-police) bodies skipped by D1/D2, the pusher keeps IDM off the body at pass.push_speed and the TTC switch makes it Dynamic. Headless R1 (car left at the box hub, player facing it) stayed RED on seeds 1/7 (146 s): the autopilot crawl (follow_speed from rest) opened the throttle 33 %, and the straight strip saw the body after it left the curved connector band.

R-A push, attempt 2 (full push speed, any loose body in the box pushable, no at-start re-pick for dynamic cars, no give-up or lost abandon at the box): seed 7 138->72 s worst stand, seed 1 still 138 s. Two causes of the same class (box locked in view): a braked sedan cannot be shoved sideways (drive 6.9 kN vs tyre grip ~16 kN; the pusher rams in reverse/forward cycles and backs into its follower), and walkers pinned on the crosswalk between the pusher and the left car hold both cars (TASK-036 walk avoidance). Stop rule: fallback R-B.

Applied fallback R-B and reverted all R-A code: the stuck cheat also removes a car nobody drives standing in (or within a car length of) a junction box when the player is farther than bubble.stuck_in_view_distance (40 m, data) or only a corner of it is in frame. R1 stays RED within 40 m and is reported; headless R1 rows are #[ignore]d with the reason. Alternative rejected: a kinematic bulldozer push (pinned bodies get driven through, the G1 pass-through class by construction).

Phantom claim fix (review MAJOR 1): one helper clear_ai_state used by abandon() and on_hijack, and snapshot_road derives claims only for is_ai() cars; G8 row a_hijacked_passer_claims_nothing asserts both separately (flip each: RED on its own assertion; both removed: the oncoming car stops at x 21). Alternative rejected: only one of the two defenses (a single flip would then have no independent gate).

R1 main-vs-branch: the stopped car is snapped by BRP onto the spot target (heading kept) after the scripted drive, re-checked after 1.5 s, so both builds leave it at the same spot; alternative not taken: the script's own drive_to reach (the first main run left the car 7 m off at (8.9,-74.9), outside the box, and two branch runs were knocked 3-5 m off after a single snap). Runs whose car moved off target are kept as invalid_* and rerun.

R1 comparison ran a third run at spot B on both builds because the branch's two B runs split 11 vs 0 cars over 30 s; alternative not taken: judging B from the two-run median alone (5.5 vs 0), which one outlier would dominate.

Bailing cars drop the pass claim by deriving claims only for Kinematic/Dynamic modes in snapshot_road, not by calling clear_ai_state on the Bailing transition as the orchestrator note named. Probe: clear_ai_state on a kinematic passer out at lateral -3.25 moves it 3.25 m sideways in one tick (lateral reset to 0, the path pose snaps back), which beside the obstacle is a kinematic pass-through. Alternative rejected: clear_ai_state with lateral kept (manoeuvre None then steers it back unchecked).

Give-up leader test: a strip on the lane line from the nose, 2 x idm.min_gap long (not 1 x): a queued car rests at the jam gap, and a threshold equal to the IDM rest point misses the leader (TASK-016 lesson; strip C uses the same margin). Off path = the footprint reaches beyond half the lane pitch (left_gap, else the car width) from the path line, which for an aligned car is |lateral| > lane slack.

Binding rule vs 'G3 rows stay green' conflict: b3 (a dummy pressed at the bumper, on its path) and G3 (e) blocked (a queued car off its lane) relied on give-up; under the rule both must wait Dynamic. Re-anchored: b3 removes the dummy after PRESSED_S 20 s and asserts no give-up while pressed plus drive-on after; (e) asserts the queued blocked car waits; give-up side moved to new row e_off_path_car_with_nothing_ahead_gives_up. Alternative not taken: exempt character leaders from the rule (keeps the old b3 but contradicts 'a car or body').

Recovery on connectors (drop on_lane, scale lateral by 1/(1-s/len), refuse near the connector end) did not move any failing number: the Dynamic box holder in c_character_in_the_lane (53.5 s) is kept Dynamic by pinned walkers within the recovery sweep (nobody_coming), and G4's 77/95.5/100 s stay. Reverted. Under the new give-up rule the Dynamic <= 30 s bound fails in c and in the three G4 correctness rows: give-up was the breaker of those locks.

R1 control run branch_fix2_control marked invalid and rerun: the scripted 150 m drive (leave=0) left the car at (-13.7, -92.8), 14 m from the junction, so it was a leave next to the box, not a control (QA's controls ended 100+ m away). Kept as r1/invalid_branch_fix2_control_car_near_box.

G4 extra row: its extra-car MAX_STOP bound moved into a new ignored seed_1_car_behind_the_body_leaves_liveness row with the Dynamic bound (extra car stands 100 s, same in-view lock class, TASK-037). Alternative not taken: keep the extra bound in the correctness row, which stays RED and contradicts option A.

Cause (c) Dynamic bound scoped by position: scene lane band from 15 m before its start to its stop line, lateral -1.7..3.25 m (right = curb shove). The node-141 holder (Connector 1296, lane 462->510) sits 6 m before the lane start, 2.5 m left, so it is printed. Alternative not taken: classify by TrafficCar.segment (StandClock keeps positions only; a new segment track adds more test machinery).

QA round 2 counter-example run: after the bump, the player's car was placed by BRP 0.2 m behind the bumped car (inside recovery skin 0.4 m) with a 1.5 s W hold instead of 4 s, to test 'on-lane, not led, pressed -> Dynamic forever'. Alternative not taken: driving into contact by keys only (the 4 s hold shoved the bumped car 50 m into a box in the plain tourist run).
